examples.text: Damit die Maske möglichst eng am Gesicht anliegt und die Viren somit schlechter durch Lücken entkommen können, ist es wichtig, den Mundschutz … weit über das Kinn zu ziehen und nicht mit den Händen zu berühren.
examples.translation: Pour que le masque soit le plus près possible du visage et que les virus puissent ainsi plus difficilement s'échapper par les interstices, il est important de tirer le masque … largement sur le menton et de ne pas le toucher avec les mains.

examples.text: Um die steifen Vatermörder, in die sich sein Kinn schmiegte, war die seidene Krawatte geschlungen, die dick und breit den ganzen Ausschnitt der buntfarbigen Weste ausfüllte …
examples.translation: Autour du rigide faux col, entre les pointes duquel s’insérait son menton, s’enroulait, épaisse et large, la cravate de soie, emplissant toute l’échancrure du gilet bigarré…

examples.text: It is worth noting that on the eighth day he was strong enough to “chin” himself six times in succession, though previous to the fasting treatment he had never in his life been able to do this more than once or twice.

glosses: To punch or hit (someone), especially on the chin (part of the body).

examples.text: He told me once that he used to be scared to death every time he started in a hard game for fear he’d get badly injured. Said it wasn’t until someone had jabbed him in the nose or ‘chinned’ him that he forgot to be scared.

examples.text: Conspicuous in the front rank of “the music” was Joe Lippett, chinning his fife […]

examples.text: I was too tired to argue; I chinned the valve three or four times, felt a blast blistering my face.

glosses: To indicate or point toward (someone or something) with one's chin.
